children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Friday.
NOTE: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply/demand report is due for release at 11 a.m. CDT (1600 GMT).
WHEAT - Down 2 to 3 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat
fell as market participants continued to monitor Black Sea tensions and grain export disruption in the key grain production region.
Traders were also awaiting results from the USDA's monthly supply and demand report.
The run-up to the USDA supply and demand forecasts on Friday encouraged profit-taking by investors, who have built up a large long position in wheat.
The USDA reported net weekly export sales of wheat for the week ended September 3 at 196,700 metric tons.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 2 cents at 7.39-1/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last 3-1/2 cents lower to $8.15-1/4 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 3/4 cents lower to $7.61-3/4 a bushel.
CORN - Down 2 to 5 cents per bushel
CBOT corn
futures dipped on Friday, as traders awaited USDA's supply and demand report, which is being seen as a gauge of the impact of hot, dry weather on the U.S. corn crop.
The USDA reported net weekly export sales of corn for the week ended September 3 at 1,872,700 metric tons.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 3-3/4 cents to $5.30 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 9 to 11 cents per bushel
CBOT soybean futures
dropped after notching multi-year highs in the last session amid China's purchase of U.S. beans before the upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 272,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans to China and another 206,500 tons to undisclosed destinations, all for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year that began on September 1.
The USDA reported net weekly export sales of soybeans for the week ended September 3 at 2,634,900 metric tons.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 11 cents at $13.21-1/4 per bushel.
